text:
incident-bot: PAGE: High-severity - GPU capacity exhaustion in aws-eu-west-1. Autoscaler failing to provision new nodes due to cloud account GPU quota limit. Queue growth observed in inference-requests (Redis). Customers may see increased latency and errors. Pager on: maya. Please ack and triage. Docs: <https://console.redwood/internal/incidents/3642109999>

maya: acked. I'm on it. grabbing metrics and logs now.

ryan: +1 — can you post current queue length and error rates? I can start quota request with AWS if we need, but need spike justification.

maya: metrics from the last 15m: 
- inference-queue length: 18k -> 36k (growing) 
- 95p latency (text-gen): 820ms -> 3.1s 
- error rate (429/503 from serving runtime): 0.6% -> 4.2% 
- available GPU nodes in eu-west-1 pool: 2 free, requested 48 but cloud returned 0 new nodes (quota).

lee: what about autoscaler logs? any sign of throttles or API errors?

maya: grabbing autoscaler controller logs. snippet: 
```
I0325 12:04:19.123 controller.go:178] Scaling up target=redwood-worker-gpu count=48
E0325 12:04:19.456 cloudprovider.go:342] CreateInstances: API error: UnsupportedOperation: RequestID abcdef - ResourceQuotaExceeded: You have reached the GPU resource limit for this account in eu-west-1
```

sam: that's the quota hit. AWS is refusing capacity. We'll need either quota increase or fallback. Quota increase usually ~2-6 hours for urgent request, sometimes faster with sales/AE.

emily: support update: we have 3 customers seeing elevated error rates; one (AcmeCorp) is hitting timeouts and has opened a ticket. They are on a critical workflow.

maya: immediate mitigations we can try: 
- reroute high-traffic customers to us-east-1 / eu-west-2 if capacity there exists.
- bring up smaller GPU instances that consume fewer vGPU units (if allowed) and increase replica count.
- failover to CPU-based pods for lower-priority workloads (batching + CPU fallback).
- apply token-bucket throttling for free/low-tier traffic to reduce queue.

ryan: I can open quota case with AWS now, marking it urgent + business-impacting. Louisa in BD can escalate — pinged. Meanwhile I can check other regions for spare capacity.

lee: checked eu-west-2 and eu-central: eu-west-2 has 24 spare GPUs available right now; eu-central has 0. We can try cross-region routing but that adds ~60-120ms to p95 for affected customers.

maya: actioning step 1: add temporary routing rule to route requests for selected customers to eu-west-2. updating routing config.

maya: patch applied. sample commands: 
```
# change routing for customer AcmeCorp to eu-west-2
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood/internal/routing" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" -d '{"customer_id":"acmecorp","preferred_region":"eu-west-2"}'
```

maya: routing changes took effect. AcmeCorp p95 latency dropped 1.2s -> 1.4s and error rate back down to 0.5%. queue for their requests drained.

sam: great. For global traffic spike we still need capacity. Can we bring up smaller instance type? Maybe g5.xlarge equivalent: fewer GPUs but might fit under current quota because quota counts per GPU SKU differently. I'll check instance family quotas.

ryan: contacted AWS support: case #AWS-123456 - requesting temporary quota bump for GPU vCPUs in eu-west-1. Asked for 200 GPUs immediate increase citing active incidents. Assigned to support engineer.

lee: in parallel: propose throttling free-tier traffic by 4x and rerouting heavy-CPU fallback jobs to CPU pool. Maya, can you apply rate-limit rule?

maya: applied soft throttling rule to free tier (token bucket - 10 req/s per org -> 2.5 req/s). Observed queue ingress drop ~30%.

maya: status update at +22m: overall queue growth slowed, total queue now 18k -> 24k (stabilizing). Autoscaler still failing to provision in eu-west-1 due to quota.

emily: I've messaged affected customers with initial incident notice: "We're experiencing capacity constraints in eu-west-1 affecting inference latency and errors. We're routing affected traffic and applying throttles. No data exposure. We'll update in 30 minutes."

sam: long-term mitigation idea: enable autoscaler fallback to launch more replicas on available smaller GPU instance types or distribute across regions automatically. We should add a runbook item.

ryan: AWS case update: support engineer says they'll expedite but no firm ETA. Asked to provide telemetry proving burst and customer impact (we provided dashboards and customer ticket links).

maya: creating incident timeline & runbook edits. quick notes for handoff: 
- root cause: AWS account GPU quota exhausted for eu-west-1. Autoscaler attempted to provision 48 GPU nodes; cloud API returned ResourceQuotaExceeded.
- impact: increased latency and 4xx/5xx errors for ~10% of requests in region. 3 customers flagged.
- mitigations taken: 
  1) rerouted high-priority customers to eu-west-2 (reduced impact to those customers).
  2) soft-throttled free-tier traffic (-75%) to reduce ingestion.
  3) started CPU fallback for low-priority batch jobs.
  4) opened AWS support case #AWS-123456 and pinged BD for escalation.
- next actions (owner): 
  * ry an: own AWS escalation (in progress).
  * lee: check infra quotas and feasibility of small-instance fallback; implement autoscaler fallback policy.
  * maya: keep routing and throttles in place, update customers.

ryan: FYI — I spun up cross-region placement groups for ephemeral capacity in eu-west-2 to absorb more traffic if needed. Also adding a flag to routing to prefer eu-west-2 for non-compliance-sensitive tenants.

emily: support will prepare a post to customers with ETA and short remediation steps.

maya: current status at +55m: queue trending down to 16k; error rate falling to 1.1%; p95 latency 1.6s. Autoscaler still blocked in eu-west-1. AWS case pending.

sam: recommend follow-up: 
- formal runbook update to include quota-check preflight in autoscaler logic.
- add synthetic alarms for quota exhaustion (cloud quota usage > 80% -> page and runbook).

lee: agreed. I'll draft autoscaler change: attempt smaller instance types and retry with exponential backoff on quota errors. Add canary to test path.

maya: preparing handoff notes for next on-call. Leaving the channel open but will hand over in 10m.

maya: HANDOFF -> next on-call: ryan (starting shift). summary: ongoing cross-region routing to eu-west-2, throttles in place, AWS case #AWS-123456 open, queue improving but autoscaler still failing in eu-west-1. Contact list: ry an (aws escalation), lee (autoscaler work), sam (fallback plan), emily (customer comms).

ryan: took handoff. I'll continue AWS escalation and monitor queue. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 3642109999 transitioned to "monitoring". Please update incident doc when resolved or if escalation changes.
